free_tier.stated: Packages larger than 150 MB or single files larger than 20 MB (in the case of GitHub) are not supported by default; a higher limit can be requested by opening an issue in the repository.

per_object_cap.stated: single files larger than 20 MB (in the case of GitHub) are not supported by default

retention.stated: Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion. We do not accept removal requests simply because a package or version was unpublished, deleted upstream, or is no longer needed.

egress.terms: using jsDelivr CDN is free, there are no limits on bandwidth or number of requests

tooling: Plain GET on cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/<pkg>@<ver>/<path> and /gh/<owner>/<repo>@<ref>/<path>. No client needed. Cache-purge API exists (email-gated).
chaining: Chains onto npm packages or GitHub repositories: assets published to npm or GitHub releases can be served via jsDelivr edge URLs with 1-year immutable caching and unmetered egress.

limits.value: single files larger than 20 MB (in the case of GitHub), default limit

limits_note: 150 MB per npm package, 20 MB per single GitHub file (both default, raisable via GitHub issue). Rate limiting applies to purge, not to reads. Enforcement is the technical risk, not the capability.
reliability_note: Retention is stronger than the origin: 'Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion. We do not accept removal requests simply because a package or version was unpublished, deleted upstream, or is no longer needed.' Once a URL has been fetched it keeps working after you delete the npm package. That is a genuine cold-archive property. Counter-risk: a 150 MB package cap means a naive >150 MB npm tarball 403s ('Package size exceeded the configured limit of 150 MB') even though npm itself accepted it.
confidence_note: The jsDelivr README was read on 2026-11-09 and states the package and file size limits.
